newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TARTU BREWERY TO EXPAND AS EYES RUSSIA, UKRAINE.
newsitem.headline: TARTU BREWERY TO EXPAND AS EYES RUSSIA, UKRAINE.

text.p: Beer-maker Tartu Brewery, owned 15 percent by Finnish Olvi, plans to take one third of the Estonian market, has opened an office in St Petersburg and is also considering the Ukrainian market.

"We have 25 percent of the market now, for the long-term we are looking for one third of the Estonian market with the Saaremaa brewery over one to two years," Tartu board member Aho Anttila told Reuters.
"Beyond that we can either expand in Estonia or go elsewhere," he added.
Net turnover for 1996 was 174.2 million kroons and turnover in 1997 is planned at 252 million kroons. No profit figures were ready as they have not been finalised.
Anttila earlier told Reuters that the company will issue around 25 percent of its shares this year and will seek a listing on the main list of the stock market.
Saku, owned by Baltic Beverage, currently dominates the Estonian market. Baltic Beverage is a joint venture of Hartwall and Pripps, owned by Norway's Orkla and Volvo.
Anttila said that Tartu brewery has opened a subsidiary in St Petersburg and was targetting growth in Ukraine.
"The subsidiary will do import and marketing work. By the end of 1998, 50 percent of our sales will be abroad, mostly beers and long drinks," he said.
"In April or May, most likely May, we will open in the Ukraine as well," he added.
Purchasing manager Mart Haldma said that investments of 50 million kroons were made last year and the same amount of investments was planned for this year.
Recent investments were made in Spring 1996 to install a modern filtration system and in 1996 this summer the company installed a new pasteurisation system.
